channel.title: HAT MI Daily - Macro and Industries
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel says the ECB will almost inevitably raise interest rates again in December, its third rise in 2026, after it held its deposit rate at 2.5% at its last meeting, Commercial Times reports.
item.description:
Commercial Times reports that, according to Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel, the European Central Bank will almost inevitably raise interest rates again in December, which would be its third rate increase in 2026. At its last policy meeting the ECB kept its benchmark deposit rate unchanged at 2.5%, citing that rapid inflation has not yet taken root, and policy officials believe the pause in rate rises is likely temporary. Nagel believes that inflation is approaching the ECB's "negative" scenario, in which price pressures would be higher than the figures the bank projected in September. The row does not give the date of the December meeting, the size of a rise, the inflation figures behind the scenario or the views of other Governing Council members beyond the reference to policy officials.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports one policymaker's expectation from one outlet, not a decision. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a further rise would raise borrowing costs in the euro area, which bear on mortgage rates, construction financing and investment in plants. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, demand from construction and manufacturing is sensitive to financing costs, so a rise could weigh on new building and equipment orders, while the row gives no figures on either. Points that may be worth considering include euro-area inflation data before the December meeting, other Governing Council members' statements and the reaction of mortgage and construction financing rates.

Commercial Times

item.title: A confidential draft declaration for the 20 November EU–UK summit would create a free trade area for farm and food products and link the two emissions trading systems, Handelsblatt reports.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that, according to a confidential draft joint declaration for the European-British summit on 20 November 2026, the EU and the UK are on the verge of a far-reaching agreement to reduce trade barriers. Both sides want to create a common free trade area for agricultural and food products and abolish most border controls for these goods. They also plan to link their emissions trading systems and mutually recognise CO2 certificates to avoid new levies on emission-intensive imports, and a new mobility programme would let young people live, study and work in the other economic area for up to three years, with a time limit and a limited number of participants. The Guardian reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is to meet European counterparts in Brussels on 20 November, that officials have all but agreed three deals that would let farmers sell freely to the EU and travellers take animals abroad more easily, that parts will not be in place until 2028, and that Burnham said the agreement would boost the UK economy by GBP 17 billion, an increase of 0.4%, the row giving no period or base. The rows do not give the terms of the emissions trading link, how the new levies on emission-intensive imports would be treated, any provisions on chemicals or manufactured goods, or the positions of EU member states.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a draft and an expectation, not an agreement. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, linking carbon markets and recognising certificates could affect how emission-intensive goods, which include some chemical products, are priced when traded between the two areas. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the rows describe the farm and food and carbon elements and say nothing on industrial goods, so any effect on raw materials or construction products would depend on terms the rows do not give. Points that may be worth considering include the published declaration after 20 November, the treatment of levies on emission-intensive imports and the dates when each element applies.

Handelsblatt | The Guardian

item.title: The European Commission plans to amend single-market rules on vehicle type approval, foreign subsidies, forced labour and trade secrets to cut reliance on nations such as China, in a package due by mid-December, Commercial Times and Lianhe Zaobao report.
item.description:
Commercial Times reports, citing informed sources, that the Commission will amend regulations on motor vehicle type approval and foreign subsidies to address economic security risks from certain imported products more effectively while reducing regulatory barriers for suppliers and companies from like-minded countries. It also plans to amend the forced labour regulation and the Trade Secrets Directive to help European companies diversify supply chains within the internal market and to raise the threshold for high-risk suppliers entering it. The measures are to be included in a package that the EU plans to announce by mid-December, and the EU's trade deficit with China reached EUR 360 billion last year and is expected to keep widening. Lianhe Zaobao attributes the report to informed sources cited by Bloomberg, describes single market rules worth EUR 18 trillion, says the aim is to reduce reliance on nations such as China and adds that the package will include a diversification tool to guide companies towards other sources of supply. The rows do not say which products or suppliers count as high-risk, what the thresholds would be, whether chemicals or construction materials are covered or how member states have reacted.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a plan from unnamed sources, not a proposal. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, changes that raise the threshold for suppliers judged high-risk, while easing entry for suppliers from like-minded countries, describe a shift in the conditions under which imports from China and other countries can enter the EU market. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the changes named relate to vehicles, subsidies, labour and trade secrets, so any effect on raw materials, resins or construction products would depend on the scope of the final text, which the rows do not give. Points that may be worth considering include the Commission's package in December, the definition of high-risk suppliers and the sectors named.

Commercial Times | Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: US networks project that Democrats win a House majority in the 3 November midterms, while reports differ on the Senate, with Handelsblatt citing rising chances and The Standard saying Democrats won both chambers.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that, according to projections by US television channels, Republicans lose their majority in the House of Representatives, that Democrats have increasing chances of regaining control of the Senate, and that from January Democrats could start investigations of the president and his administration in the House. Süddeutsche Zeitung reports that, according to estimates relayed from NBC News and CBS News, Democrat James Talarico won the Texas Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton, the third Senate seat the Democrats are expected to take from the Republicans after North Carolina and South Carolina, while Commercial Times lists four expected Democratic Senate gains, in Kansas, Ohio, Texas and South Carolina. Commercial Times reports that CNN, NBC and CBS projected a Democratic House majority, that CBS predicts at least 218 House seats for the Democrats, and that US stock index futures fell as investors anticipated a Democratic majority in Congress, with Nasdaq 100 futures down over 2%, the row giving no baseline. The Standard reports that Democrats captured majorities in both the Senate and the House. A Globe and Mail commentary, which speaks of the Republicans' loss of control of both chambers, cites experts saying that tariffs issued under the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and the Trade Act of 1974 are on sound legal footing, that without a 60-seat Senate majority these laws are not going to be amended and Democrats do not want them changed, and that the tariff war with Canada will continue and could even get worse. A Financial Times column, written before the results, expects a Democratic sweep of both houses to bring more congressional oversight of tariff actions and a divided Congress to leave elevated tariffs in place. The rows do not give final seat counts for either chamber, a Senate call by the networks, the date the new Congress sits or a White House reaction.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report projections, not a final result, and the views on tariffs are commentary. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a House controlled by the opposition can hold hearings and investigations and use its budget powers, while the Globe and Mail commentary describes the two tariff statutes it names as unlikely to be amended, so the rows point to continued tariffs with more scrutiny rather than to a reversal. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, US tariffs on imports and on trading partners such as Canada affect the cost of raw materials and of inputs for construction and manufacturing, and the rows give no tariff rates or product lists. Points that may be worth considering include the Senate result, any House hearings or votes on tariff actions from January and tariff announcements by the White House after the election.

Handelsblatt | Süddeutsche Zeitung | Commercial Times | Commercial Times | The Standard | The Globe and Mail | The Financial Times

item.title: Chinese brands took 22.5% of Norway's new car registrations in October against 16.9% a year earlier, People's Daily reports, and BYD's overseas shipments rose 102.8% year on year to 170,194 vehicles, MarketScreener reports.
item.description:
People's Daily Online, citing the Norwegian Road Federation, reports that new passenger car registrations in Norway rose 41.2% year on year to 15,725 units in October, of which Chinese brands accounted for 22.5% against 16.9% in October 2025, with 3,534 registrations against 1,879. Cinco Días reports that passenger vehicle registrations in Spain rose 1.8% to 98,487 units in October, the best October since 2007 and the fifth consecutive monthly rise, helped by electrified vehicles, 31.5% of registrations, and by deliveries from Chinese brands; BYD was the fifth best-selling brand and its Atto 2 the third most registered model, with 1,911 units. Le Dauphiné Libéré, citing AutoScout24.fr, reports that registrations of Chinese cars on France's used car market rose 69% in September, the row not stating the comparison period for the total, with MG at 2,389 units (up 72% year on year) and BYD at 644 (up 66.4%). MarketScreener reports that BYD sold 490,168 vehicles in October, up 11% year on year, and that overseas shipments were nearly 35% of its monthly sales. The rows do not give the Chinese brands' share in Spain or other EU markets, prices, the tariff treatment of the cars or plans for production in Europe.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report registrations and shipments by brand, not vehicle production or materials. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a rising share for Chinese brands in Norway, higher Chinese-brand deliveries in Spain and more Chinese used cars registered in France, together with doubled overseas shipments at BYD, describe a shift in who supplies European buyers, to the extent that BYD's shipments go to Europe, which the rows do not say. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, to the extent that cars sold in Europe are built in China, which the rows do not say, their bonding and sealing is done there, so a larger share could move part of the demand for automotive bonding and sealing materials between regions; the rows give no figures for materials. Points that may be worth considering include the November registration data, any EU decision on tariffs or local content for Chinese-built cars and announcements of European production by Chinese brands.

People's Daily Online | Cinco Días | Le Dauphiné Libéré | MarketScreener

item.title: The BVSE Material Flow Picture reports German production of fossil-based plastics at 8.64 million tonnes in 2025 against 8.82 million in 2023 and processing at 12.22 million against 12.85 million, with post-consumer recyclates at 13.6% of processing.
item.description:
BVSE (Bundesverband Sekundärrohstoffe und Entsorgung) reports in its Material Flow Picture Plastics in Germany 2025 that production, processing, consumption and waste generation decreased compared with 2023 while the move to a circular economy is progressing only slowly. Production of fossil-based plastics fell to 8.64 million tonnes from 8.82 million, processing, including recyclates and reused by-products, to 12.22 million tonnes from 12.85 million, and consumption to 10.93 million tonnes from 11.25 million. Post-consumer plastic waste fell slightly for the first time since the survey began, to 5.52 million tonnes from 5.58 million. Recyclate production rose to 2.05 million tonnes from 2.01 million, the use of post-consumer recyclates to 1.66 million tonnes from 1.54 million, and their share of processing to 13.6% from 12.0%. About two thirds of processed plastics, 8 million tonnes, go into durable applications such as vehicle and mechanical engineering, electrical applications, household and sports goods and civil engineering, and about a third, 4 million tonnes, into short-lived uses such as packaging and agriculture. BVSE says that recyclate production, use and the recycling rate are developing positively but that the dynamics have slowed significantly compared with earlier survey periods. The row does not give figures for 2024, the split within these two groups, the reasons for the slowdown or any outlook.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports volumes for two survey years from one association. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, lower production, processing and consumption of plastics describes weaker demand for polymers in Germany, while a rising recyclate share changes the mix of materials that other products work with. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, plastics are bonded, sealed and coated in vehicles, machinery, electrical products and building products, so lower volumes could reduce demand for bonding and coating materials, and a higher recyclate share could change the surfaces and processes involved; the row gives no figures for materials used in bonding, sealing or coating. Points that may be worth considering include 2024 and 2026 volumes, the application split and the reasons BVSE gives for the slowdown.

BVSE

item.title: Handelsblatt reports Brent at about USD 106 on 3 November, about 1.5% above Monday, after consistent media reports of a US attack on the Iranian island of Gheschm, while MarketScreener reported Brent down more than 1% on the same day.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that, following reports of renewed US military attacks on targets in Iran, Brent crude for January delivery traded at around USD 106 on 3 November, about 1.5% higher than on Monday, and that according to consistent media reports the US attacked targets on the Iranian island of Gheschm in the Strait of Hormuz, where a Revolutionary Guard position was reportedly attacked after a missile was fired from there at a US aircraft. Commercial Times reports that on 2 November both benchmarks initially fell by over 8%, with West Texas Intermediate falling below USD 100, and rebounded by over 1% on 3 November, with WTI at USD 97.6 and Brent at USD 105.8; it adds that, according to the report, the outside world believes the US-Iran talks do not mean the end of the conflict and that depleted global energy inventories will make price swings more severe. MarketScreener reports that Brent fell more than 1% on 3 November, extending declines after a sharp drop in the previous session, as investors followed developments on a peace deal, and Arab News reports Trump saying on 2 November that a deal "could happen". LiveMint reports Brent above USD 106 and WTI around USD 95 as the US results arrived; the rows do not say at what times the quotes were taken. The rows do not give a closing level, a US or Iranian statement on the reported attack, damage or casualties, or shipping data for the strait.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report price quotes whose times are not stated and one report of an attack, not a change in oil flows. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, crude and its products set the cost of many raw materials with a lag, and renewed strikes alongside talks keep the direction of prices open, as the opposite readings in the rows from the same day show. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, higher oil prices could raise the cost of resins, solvents and freight with a delay, while the rows give no prices for these. Points that may be worth considering include an official account of the reported attack, Brent after the US election result and shipping data for the strait.

Handelsblatt | Commercial Times | MarketScreener | Arab News | LiveMint

item.title: Schaeffler plans to cut another 3,460 jobs in Europe, 2,660 in Germany, and to close four German sites, with an expected EUR 300 million annual gain from 2030 and one-off costs of about EUR 480 million, Handelsblatt and Wallstreet:online report.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that the automotive and industrial supplier is tightening its austerity course with another cost-cutting programme, announced in Herzogenaurach. The four German closures include the Dortmund plant, with currently 430 employees, and the Morbach site, with 160 employees; activities are to cease at the Berlin site, with around 270 employees, and the Schwalbach site is to close, where a large part of the roughly 385 employees are to move to Frankfurt and around 190 jobs are affected. Toolmaking at Höchstadt is to cease, special machine construction at Erlangen and Schweinfurt is to be adjusted, and capacity and structural adjustments are planned at Herzogenaurach, Bühl, Höchstadt, Nuremberg and Regensburg. Wallstreet:online reports that the annual result is expected to improve by EUR 300 million from 2030 and that Chief Executive Klaus Rosenfeld estimates one-off costs of around EUR 480 million. The rows do not give a timetable for the cuts, the products or production lines affected, the number of jobs already cut or Schaeffler's view of vehicle demand.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a company plan, not the state of the German automotive supplier industry. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, an automotive and industrial supplier closing four sites and cutting 2,660 German jobs describes cost pressure at one company that could also reach other component makers, and the savings horizon of 2030 suggests the company expects the pressure to last. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, automotive and industrial component plants use bonding, sealing and coating materials, so closures and capacity adjustments could change volumes and supplier choices at the affected sites; the rows name no materials. Points that may be worth considering include the timetable for the closures, other suppliers' restructuring announcements and German vehicle production data.

Handelsblatt | Wallstreet:online

item.title: The Automotive Distributors and Mobility Association (ODMD) reports that Türkiye's passenger car and light commercial vehicle market fell 30.84% year on year in October to 80,334 units and 15.33% in January–October, Hürriyet Daily News writes.
item.description:
Hürriyet Daily News, citing ODMD, reports that passenger car sales in Türkiye fell 28.4% year on year in October to 64,939 units and light commercial vehicle sales fell 39.52% to 15,395 units. In January–October the combined market fell 15.33% to 883,799 units, with passenger cars down 16.85% to 692,916 units and light commercial vehicles down 9.28% to 190,883 units. Electric vehicle sales edged down 0.4% year on year to 14,467 units in October, 22.3% of passenger car sales, and were 135,979 units in January–October, down 8.3%. Togg sold 44,187 vehicles in the first ten months and Tesla 6,118 units. The row does not give the reasons for the fall, the October 2025 base, sales by brand for October, or domestic production and export figures.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports sales, not production, and gives no cause for the fall. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a fall of this size in a single month, with a smaller fall over ten months, describes demand that weakened sharply in October, and the cause would decide whether it is temporary. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, vehicles use bonding, sealing and coating materials in assembly and in components, so lower sales could reduce orders along the supply chain in Türkiye if production follows sales, while the row gives no production or export data. Points that may be worth considering include the November registration data, Turkish vehicle production and export figures and any change in vehicle taxes or credit terms.

Hürriyet Daily News

item.title: Wallstreet:online reports that European consumers and companies pay over USD 30 per million British thermal units for gas against about USD 3 in the US, a gap it says the Iran war has driven to a historic extent.
item.description:
Wallstreet:online reports that the Iran war is exacerbating an imbalance that could permanently weaken Europe's industry. European consumers and companies pay over USD 30 per million British thermal units (mBtu) for natural gas, while the raw material costs only around USD 3 in the US, and the article says the price difference has been driven to a historic extent by the Iran war. According to Bloomberg data, gas in Europe and Asia was at times 12 times as expensive as in North America, which the article says did not happen during the 2022 energy crisis or after the Fukushima disaster in 2011. Last week US gas prices briefly reached a two-year low of USD 2.50 per mBtu, and prices in Canada are lower still at around USD 1.50. The row does not name the benchmarks behind the USD 30 and USD 3 figures, give the date of the quotes or the period of the 12-times gap, or give the share of gas in the cost of chemical products.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The row reports price levels and a ratio from one outlet, with only the ratio attributed to Bloomberg data. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, natural gas is both a fuel and a feedstock for parts of the chemical industry, so a gas price in Europe many times that in North America can shift the relative cost position of European producers against North American ones. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, higher European energy cost could pass into the price of resins, polymers and other raw materials made in Europe, and imports from lower-cost regions could gain a price advantage; the row names no products. Points that may be worth considering include the benchmark behind the USD 30 figure, European gas prices in the coming weeks and announcements of capacity changes at European producers.

Wallstreet:online

item.title: Ifo says Germany's chemical industry business climate fell to minus 5.9 in October from plus 3.0 in September and expectations to minus 13.8 from minus 1.5, while demand and new orders rose, Handelsblatt and MarketScreener report.
item.description:
MarketScreener reports that the Ifo Institute's business climate index for Germany's chemical industry slipped below zero again in October, to minus 5.9 points from a seasonally adjusted 3 points in September, erasing two months of improvement, as structural challenges overshadowed support from Middle East-related supply disruptions. Business expectations fell to minus 13.8 points from minus 1.5. Handelsblatt, citing Ifo industry expert Anna Wolf, reports that restructuring and site closures in the chemical industry are causing concern and that companies assess their current business situation less positively. It adds that demand rose in October compared with September and new orders rose, that companies intend to expand production and plan to raise prices further, and that capacity use was 76.6%, up from 73.4% in July. MarketScreener adds that German chemical companies have stepped up cost-saving and restructuring against a weak economic backdrop and growing competition from Asian producers. The rows do not give the number of companies surveyed, the index for earlier months, the sites that are closing or the size of the planned price rises.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The rows report a survey index, expectations and survey answers on demand, orders, capacity use and price plans, not measured output or prices. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a climate index below zero with sharply lower expectations describes a sector that expects weaker conditions, and the rows also report higher demand, new orders and capacity use. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, German chemical producers supply raw materials and intermediates, so site closures and restructuring could change which inputs are made where, and planned price rises could pass into raw material costs; the rows name no products. Points that may be worth considering include Ifo's November reading, the sites and products affected by closures and the size of the planned price increases.

MarketScreener | Handelsblatt
